body: ok-outcome-after-declined-second-plan: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/skills/ok/SKILL.md:60 (step 4.5) answers an abort of the first plan with 'write nothing and ask nothing else. Skip steps 5 and 6, and report the outcome declined; stays on v<stamped>'. SKILL.md:72 (step 5.4, as the fixer built it) answers an abort of the second plan with 'write nothing more and go on to step 6; the report lists each DESTRUCTIVE: line the owner turned down, and the outcome reads trued up; plan steps pending: <d>'; SKILL.md:129 repeats that outcome. The filed facts hold. Mechanism: pass one has already applied and re-stamped the layer before step 5 runs, so 'stays on v<stamped>' after a second decline would name the new version while implying nothing changed; and a second plan turns destructive in two named cases (an answer unblocks a destructive step, or an answer or amend draft changes a file pass one rendered, e.g. a lint_checks repair, which archives and rewrites each such file). A decline leaves those files as pass one rendered them, out of step with the answer just applied. Corpus: decision:true-up-asks-once-before-destructive-steps says 'On abort, true-up writes nothing, and the project stays on the suite version its stamps record' and 'All of the plan or none of it are the two states that work', and that the input questions and the wiring come after the plan runs; it is silent on a destructive plan that a post-plan answer causes. story:true-up-project-estate promises one deliberate act that never costs the owner work they wrote. Harm: none an entry covers today beyond a possible A9 report if the outcome claimed 'stays on' the old version. Options: A (as built): report trued up with the declined steps pending and run the wiring; cost: the pass ends with an answer applied to config but not to the files it renders, a part-applied state the decision's rationale warns against, until the next /ok. B: report the first plan's outcome and skip the wiring; cost: the outcome reads as unchanged though pass one's writes and stamps stand (a false report under A9's terms), and the owner loses the wiring consent the decline did not concern. C (missed by the filer): on a decline of the second plan, back out the answer or amend draft that made it destructive, so config and rendered files agree, then report the answer as declined and run the wiring; cost: one more core step, and the owner's answer is lost until the next /ok. Each option needs a sentence added to decision:true-up-asks-once-before-destructive-steps naming the second plan, so this is a promise change. Recommended: A, with the decision delta, since pass one's writes are real, the pending line tells the owner what is owed, and the next /ok re-asks; flip to C where the owner rejects ending a pass with config and rendered files out of step. Siblings: none in this batch.

plan-tests-reviews-a-whole-plan-with-one-agent: Evidence holds. plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-tests/SKILL.md:66 (step 9) files one review task, 'tasks file --role review --prompt review --agent ok-opus --key review --brief "review the plan"', under {{TEST-PLAN-REVIEW-PROMPT}} at plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-tests/core.md:336-380, whose Check list mixes per-planner checks (no story way yields two scenarios for one program, core.md:357-359; outcome text; reach through a public entry point; port/adopt) with plan-wide ones (owner answers hold, core.md:362-363). Planning is split one planner per story plus one runtime planner; review is not, so the reviewer's reading grows with the plan (linescout, v28.0.0: 485 scenarios, 108 planners, 345 calls, ~538k tokens, 44 findings over ~38 planners). Mechanism: each finding refiles the planner its site names, so one late plan-wide review sends most planners back in one wave after all planning is done. Corpus: silent on how the plan's review is split; scenario-list-decided-once says only that the owner 'approves the whole list once'; tests-check-scenarios and legacy-suites-sorted-automatically ('Sort agents read the tests in batches') bound what is reviewed, not the review's shape. Tooling the change edits: plan-tests SKILL.md step 9 and core.md's review prompt (and the planner prompts for option C). No accept-list entry; a judgment on the project's own tooling, no stated rule decides it. Options: A, one review task per planner plus one plan-wide task for cross-planner checks (duplicates, owner answers): bounded reading per task, more tasks and a second assembly of plan-wide findings; B, review in fixed-size batches of related stories: fewer tasks, but a batch still mixes planners and the batch size is arbitrary; C, move per-planner checks into each planner's prompt as a self-check before close, keep one plan-wide review: cheapest, but a self-check is the planner judging its own work, which a cold reviewer exists to avoid; also missed by the filer, A combined with C. Recommended lean: A, since it matches how planning is already split. Rule with plan-tests-caps-each-story-way-at-one-scenario-per-program (its cap is the check behind most findings; changing it changes what any split review checks) and plan-tests-approval-shows-the-whole-plan-unsorted (same large-plan scale).

plan-tests-caps-each-story-way-at-one-scenario-per-program: Evidence holds. plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-tests/core.md:27-28 (the scenario definition): 'Each story's way of giving its benefit yields at most one scenario per program that carries it'; core.md:357-359 (plan review): 'No story way yields two scenarios for one program.' The cap is a corpus commitment, not only skill text: decision:tests-check-scenarios, Choice: 'Each story way yields at most one scenario per program that carries it, and each pairing of part, class, and harm yields one'; its Rationale ties the cap to a bounded suite ('bounded by the stories and the runtime parts, not by how many tests an agent thinks to write') and 'A second test of a covered scenario is a duplicate; the test sprint deletes both'. So option A changes what the corpus commits to and needs a corpus delta to that decision, not only a skill edit; the filer frames it as tooling. Mechanism: a planner that files a refusal, a variant input, or a second path through one program as its own scenario departs from the definition, the review flags it, and the session refiles the planner to fold or drop it (linescout, v28.0.0: 26 of 44 findings; e.g. a last-administrator refusal, four liveness states, six provenance checks on one record command). Harm the filer names: distinct outcomes merged into one test or left untested; no accept-list entry covers it (prose and plan shape), it is the owner's choice. Options: A, replace the cap with one scenario per distinct outcome a user or the product sees through a program, keeping only the rule against two scenarios checking one outcome: covers refusals and variants as their own scenarios; cost: the suite grows with outcomes rather than ways, weakening the 'bounded' rationale, and 'distinct outcome' needs a test a reviewer can apply; edits decision:tests-check-scenarios, core.md:27-28 and :357-359, and the planner prompts; B, keep the cap and let one scenario's test check each variant and refusal as a separate case inside it: no corpus change; cost: a scenario's text must then list its cases, and one failing case marks the whole scenario failing, so the test loop's per-scenario issue wait (scenario-list-decided-once: 'the open issue a failing scenario waits on') covers several outcomes at once; C (missed by the filer), keep the cap per way but count a refusal the story names as its own way: smallest change, but only covers refusals, not variants or states. Rule with plan-tests-reviews-a-whole-plan-with-one-agent (this cap drives most of that review's findings) and plan-tests-approval-shows-the-whole-plan-unsorted.

task-tracker-cannot-drop-an-item: Evidence holds, line numbers drifted. The tracker's item verbs are add, list, count, and set at plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tasks:1487-1512 (filed as L1486-L1505); set takes --state, --note, --key, --field (tasks:1506-1511), and cmd_item checks a new state against the pool's configured states (tasks:1106-1108, check_state); nothing removes an item or detaches it from its task. The /plan-tests assembler reads every item of a pool whatever its state (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:412-413, run_items with no --state) and keeps those whose task is a planner's latest done task (tests:513, mine = items whose task is in done), so an item a planner should not have filed stays in every assembly until that planner is refiled. The estate guide rule is now at plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/ok-planner-CLAUDE.md:498 (filed as :492): 'Never hand-edit a run file; the tracker's verbs are the only writers.' Linescout, v28.0.0: five retire items on a first plan (no stamp) refused by the assembler; the sanctioned fix was rerunning four planners (~280k tokens), and the owner approved a hand edit against the rule. Corpus: concept:task-tracker says the tracker 'keeps only what was filed' and 'decides nothing and judges nothing', and that a later reader learns 'what each task produced from the record alone'; it is silent on removing an item. A removal verb that leaves a removal event keeps the record durable; one that deletes lines would not. No accept-list entry for the project's own run (an operator workflow cost, not stored-state loss). Judgment on the project's own tooling; no stated rule decides it. Options: A, a drop verb that appends a removal event (who, why) and hides the item from later reads: one verb, every reader benefits, record kept; cost: a new event type in the run file format and the index rebuild; B, a 'dropped' state per pool that every reader skips, set through the existing item set: no new verb, but every reader (the tests assembler at tests:514, 521, 530, 532, 749, 1048, 1096; review; docs) must learn to skip it, and a reader that forgets reads a dropped item; C (missed by the filer), have the assembler refuse with a per-item message and let the session refile only the one planner with its failure in the brief, as SKILL.md step 7 already does: no tracker change, but it keeps the rerun cost the issue names. body: plan-tests-rejects-a-malformed-scenario-id-only-at-assembly: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:plan_failures (L593, check at L602-L604) refuses an id that fails SLUG = ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$ (tests L93), only when tests plan assembles. tasks item add writes any field value it is given (scripts/tasks cmd_item). SKILL.md step 7 (L58) gives one remedy, 'refile the planner whose items fail with tasks refile', and step 5 (L45) has the refile's items replace the earlier task's; step 11 (L80) lets the session write only the test sprint, its sibling files, testing.run, and issues. Rot in the filed problem: the runtime prompt does state an id shape. core.md L213-L214 ({{TEST-RUNTIME-PLANNER-PROMPT}}) says 'Name a new one runtime--<part>--<class>, with the harm's entry where one part and class carry two harms', and the harm field takes A1 to A9 (core.md L227-L228, tests checks ACCEPT_ENTRY). So the prompt itself told the planner to append 'A7', an upper-case entry the slug check refuses: runtime--query-engine--dependency-down--A7 is the prompt's own form, not a copying slip. The story prompt's form, <story slug>--<way> (core.md L137), passes. Mechanism: the prompt's naming rule and the assembly check disagree, and the only sanctioned remedy reruns the whole planner. Tooling the change edits: skills/plan-tests/core.md (runtime planner naming rule), skills/plan-tests/SKILL.md steps 5 and 7, scripts/tests plan, and possibly scripts/tasks item add (which today knows nothing of scenario pools; a per-pool field check there would be a new tracker mechanism). Corpus: decision:scenario-list-decided-once and decision:tests-check-scenarios are silent on id shape and on how planning repairs an item; decision:no-execution-engine says the tracker 'plans, gates, or judges' nothing, which weighs against option A's tracker check. A stated rule decides one part: the prompt must name a form the check accepts, so the runtime naming rule changes to a lower-case harm suffix (e.g. --a7) or drops it, under every option. Harm: cost only (about 100,000 tokens and the owner's review of 52 scenarios lost); no accept-list entry. Options: A: refuse a non-slug id at tasks item add and fix the prompt; cost: the generic tracker learns one pool's schema, against decision:no-execution-engine, or needs a new per-pool validation config. A' (missed): have tests offer a check verb the planner runs on its own items before it closes (e.g. tests plan --check-task <task>), and fix the prompt; cost: one more verb, and the planner must run it. B: keep the check at assembly and add a mechanical rename step in SKILL.md with tasks item set --field id=<new> (item set already updates fields, tasks L1102-L1114); cost: the session writes planner items, and the skill must say which failures count as mechanical. C: both A (or A') and B. Recommended: fix the prompt's naming rule (decided) plus B, since B also serves the sibling issue's mechanical fixes and needs no tracker change; flip to A' where the owner wants the planner to catch its own slip in its turn. Siblings: plan-tests-fixes-a-finding-by-rebuilding-the-planner; rule together.

body: delta-body-inner-fence-breaks-certification: A stuck issue (Stuck in converge-2026-10-22T030501), so a judgment issue; the harm still stands. The two readings disagree, which is the mechanism behind every probe in the record. The delta form ({{CORPUS-DELTA-FORM}}, plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/_shared/artifact-definitions.md:277-287) and the sprint template (skills/plan-sprint/sprint-document.md:25-39) say nothing about fencing an inline body; the round-1 four-backtick rule was backed out. Corpus: story:certify-completion, "done means the same thing for every sprint"; decision:final-form-deltas, certification "compares the two file for file" and lands a missed delta "by copying the delta's body into place verbatim", so a verbatim-landed body must certify, and the tool must count only the deltas the sprint wrote; concept:corpus-delta. The corpus decides the end state; the mechanism is the owner's choice after two send-backs. Harm, A9: review deltas lists a delta landed byte for byte as unsettled ('differs from the delta's body'), review certified prints 'item 1 (deltas): fails' and SPRINT NOT COMPLETE, and a body whose inner block holds a heading-like line makes the tool count a phantom delta or drop a real one. Options, each with the verifier's reason where a run tried it: A. The delta form requires a body holding fenced blocks to use a longer outer fence than any inner fence (CommonMark), and review refuses a markdown body whose inner fence is not shorter, naming the rule; the run never tried the refusal half; cost: sprints already written with three-backtick bodies holding blocks fail until rewritten, and the planner must follow one more form rule. B. Review reads nested fences by depth so any consistently fenced body reads whole (fix 2, inline_body on fence_depths); the confirm driver sent it back because a bare inner block pops the outer fence, so its lines read at depth 0 and a heading-like line inside splits the section, phantom delta counted, real delta dropped; cost: a bare inner fence is ambiguous under any depth reading, so B alone cannot read every body as its author meant. C. Fix 1: end the body at the last closer in the delta's span, plus the four-backtick wording; the verifier sent it back because inline_body and unfenced_lines then disagree on an info-string inner block followed by another delta, so the next delta drops out. D. Both A and B: read by depth for the info-string case, and refuse the ambiguous bare-inner-fence case naming the longer-fence rule; cost: two rules to keep in step across inline_body, section_lines, and unfenced_lines. E, the filer missed it: require the sidecar for any body holding a fenced block, and refuse such an inline body naming 'body: in the sidecar'; cost: one more file per such delta, and the refusal still needs a fence check. A call is an item in the calls pool with only site, choice, and a free-text body ({{TEST-CALL-RULE}}, plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-tests/core.md:69-78): nothing marks a call's kind, so no tool can sort calls today. Linescout, v28.0.0: ~980 KB listing, 500 scenarios, 373 calls; a session keyword sort found ~95 calls that left a behavior untested, the only group the owner needed. Corpus: decision:scenario-list-decided-once: the owner 'decides each scenario whose outcome changed or whose code is gone, and each program no story serves, and approves the whole list once'; decision:legacy-suites-sorted-automatically: 'The plan lists every test with its sort, and the owner approves it once'. Both commit to one approval of the whole list; neither says the owner reads it unsorted, so a summary with the full listing kept satisfies both. No accept-list entry (the approval rests on an improvised summary, a judgment on the project's own tooling); no stated rule decides it. Options: A, tests plan prints an approval summary (counts per story, calls sorted, those that leave a behavior untested or depart from an owner answer first and in full): owner reads one short page; cost: sorting needs a kind on each call, so it implies a call field anyway, or a heuristic sort that can misplace a call; B, each planner marks each call mechanical or owner-facing and approval shows only owner-facing calls, full listing kept in a file: precise and cheap to print; cost: a planner that misjudges hides a call from the owner, and {{TEST-CALL-RULE}} and every planner prompt change; C (missed), A built on B's field: planners tag a kind (e.g. untested-behavior, owner-answer departure, scope reading, mechanics), and the summary sorts by it, all calls still listed below. The planner prompt plans only files under the current Where (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-docs/core.md:110-116 'Per file under the Where ...'), so an Amend that moves ## Where leaves the old files unread too. plan-docs/SKILL.md:18 stops when no docspec stands. Harm: cost only (about 100,000 tokens and the owner's review of 52 scenarios lost); no accept-list entry. C: both A (or A') and B. Recommended: fix the prompt's naming rule (decided) plus B, since B also serves the sibling issue's mechanical fixes and needs no tracker change; flip to A' where the owner wants the planner to catch its own slip in its turn. Linescout, v28.0.0: ~980 KB listing, 500 scenarios, 373 calls; a session keyword sort found ~95 calls that left a behavior untested, the only group the owner needed. Corpus: decision:scenario-list-decided-once: the owner 'decides each scenario whose outcome changed or whose code is gone, and each program no story serves, and approves the whole list once'; decision:legacy-suites-sorted-automatically: 'The plan lists every test with its sort, and the owner approves it once'. Both commit to one approval of the whole list; neither says the owner reads it unsorted, so a summary with the full listing kept satisfies both. No accept-list entry (the approval rests on an improvised summary, a judgment on the project's own tooling); no stated rule decides it. Options: A, tests plan prints an approval summary (counts per story, calls sorted, those that leave a behavior untested or depart from an owner answer first and in full): owner reads one short page; cost: sorting needs a kind on each call, so it implies a call field anyway, or a heuristic sort that can misplace a call; B, each planner marks each call mechanical or owner-facing and approval shows only owner-facing calls, full listing kept in a file: precise and cheap to print; cost: a planner that misjudges hides a call from the owner, and {{TEST-CALL-RULE}} and every planner prompt change; C (missed), A built on B's field: planners tag a kind (e.g. untested-behavior, owner-answer departure, scope reading, mechanics), and the summary sorts by it, all calls still listed below. Rule with plan-tests-reviews-a-whole-plan-with-one-agent and plan-tests-caps-each-story-way-at-one-scenario-per-program (the cap change alters how many untested-behavior calls a plan produces).

retired-docspec-leaves-documentation-behind: Judgment issue about the product; the corpus is silent on who answers for documentation a docspec no longer covers. Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/docs:cmd_window (L334-L340) iterates docspec_slugs(root) only and prints 'no docspec under ... the project declares no documentation' when none stands; a retired docspec's .ok-planner/doc-state/<slug>.json and its documentation files stay tracked and nothing reads them. The planner prompt plans only files under the current Where (plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-docs/core.md:110-116 'Per file under the Where ...'), so an Amend that moves ## Where leaves the old files unread too. plan-docs/SKILL.md:18 stops when no docspec stands. Mechanism: the window and the planner both start from live docspecs, so a file no live docspec names is invisible to every documentation sprint. Corpus: story:keep-documentation-current 'bring every document my project keeps up to date ... a reader finds documentation that describes the product as it stands' (silent on whether 'keeps' means 'a live docspec declares'); decision:docspec-stamp-opens-the-window plans each docspec 'whose own text ... or documentation changed since its stamp' (silent on retired docspecs); decision:final-form-deltas 'retirement by delta is the only sanctioned way ... a docspec leaves the project's docspecs' (silent on its files); decision:documentation-sprints-write-the-documentation 'only a documentation sprint writes a project's documentation ... their builders write no documentation', which option B collides with unless that decision also names deletion by the retiring sprint. Harm: stale documentation stays in the tree describing a product that moved on; no accept-list entry needed (judgment). Options: A. The story covers orphaned documentation: plan-docs reads doc-state entries with no live docspec and each docspec's Where at its stamp, and plans drop or check items for the old files; cost: the window and the planner must reconstruct a retired order from git history and doc-state. B. The retiring or moving sprint decides the old files: the story, decision:docspec-stamp-opens-the-window, and decision:documentation-sprints-write-the-documentation say a retired docspec's files leave with that sprint; cost: a sprint's builders delete documentation, a second writer of documentation. C (filer missed): the retiring or moving sprint records the old files as a drop order the next documentation sprint executes, so only a documentation sprint touches documentation; cost: a new hand-off record between /plan-sprint and /plan-docs. No sibling issues among this batch.

plan-tests-rejects-a-malformed-scenario-id-only-at-assembly: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/tests:plan_failures (L593, check at L602-L604) refuses an id that fails SLUG = ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$ (tests L93), only when tests plan assembles. tasks item add writes any field value it is given (scripts/tasks cmd_item). SKILL.md step 7 (L58) gives one remedy, 'refile the planner whose items fail with tasks refile', and step 5 (L45) has the refile's items replace the earlier task's; step 11 (L80) lets the session write only the test sprint, its sibling files, testing.run, and issues. Rot in the filed problem: the runtime prompt does state an id shape. core.md L213-L214 ({{TEST-RUNTIME-PLANNER-PROMPT}}) says 'Name a new one runtime--<part>--<class>, with the harm's entry where one part and class carry two harms', and the harm field takes A1 to A9 (core.md L227-L228, tests checks ACCEPT_ENTRY). So the prompt itself told the planner to append 'A7', an upper-case entry the slug check refuses: runtime--query-engine--dependency-down--A7 is the prompt's own form, not a copying slip. The story prompt's form, <story slug>--<way> (core.md L137), passes. Mechanism: the prompt's naming rule and the assembly check disagree, and the only sanctioned remedy reruns the whole planner. Tooling the change edits: skills/plan-tests/core.md (runtime planner naming rule), skills/plan-tests/SKILL.md steps 5 and 7, scripts/tests plan, and possibly scripts/tasks item add (which today knows nothing of scenario pools; a per-pool field check there would be a new tracker mechanism). Corpus: decision:scenario-list-decided-once and decision:tests-check-scenarios are silent on id shape and on how planning repairs an item; decision:no-execution-engine says the tracker 'plans, gates, or judges' nothing, which weighs against option A's tracker check. A stated rule decides one part: the prompt must name a form the check accepts, so the runtime naming rule changes to a lower-case harm suffix (e.g. --a7) or drops it, under every option. Harm: cost only (about 100,000 tokens and the owner's review of 52 scenarios lost); no accept-list entry. Options: A: refuse a non-slug id at tasks item add and fix the prompt; cost: the generic tracker learns one pool's schema, against decision:no-execution-engine, or needs a new per-pool validation config. A' (missed): have tests offer a check verb the planner runs on its own items before it closes (e.g. tests plan --check-task <task>), and fix the prompt; cost: one more verb, and the planner must run it. B: keep the check at assembly and add a mechanical rename step in SKILL.md with tasks item set --field id=<new> (item set already updates fields, tasks L1102-L1114); cost: the session writes planner items, and the skill must say which failures count as mechanical. C: both A (or A') and B. Recommended: fix the prompt's naming rule (decided) plus B, since B also serves the sibling issue's mechanical fixes and needs no tracker change; flip to A' where the owner wants the planner to catch its own slip in its turn. Siblings: plan-tests-fixes-a-finding-by-rebuilding-the-planner; rule together.

plan-tests-fixes-a-finding-by-rebuilding-the-planner: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-tests/SKILL.md step 5 (L45) 'the latest done task of each planner stands, and its items replace the earlier task's'; step 7 (L58) answers an assembly failure with 'refile the planner whose items fail with tasks refile <its task> --brief "<its brief, and the failure>"'; step 9 (L66) answers each review finding the same way, then marks the finding resolved; step 10 (L70) answers an owner's change at approval the same way; step 11 (L80) lets the session write only the test sprint, its sibling files, testing.run, and issues. The planner prompts in core.md ({{TEST-STORY-PLANNER-PROMPT}} L101-L103, {{TEST-RUNTIME-PLANNER-PROMPT}}) read the story, the code, and the stamp's recorded scenarios (tests scenarios --json), never the planning run's earlier items, so a refiled planner sees the finding only in its brief and files a whole new set. The filed facts hold. Mechanism: scripts/tasks cmd_refile (L814) copies the task with a new brief and links previous; nothing carries the earlier items forward, and the scenarios pool has one state, open (SKILL.md L40), so no item can be marked dropped or folded without a pool change. tasks item set (scripts/tasks L1102-L1114) can rewrite an item's fields and state today. Tooling the change edits: skills/plan-tests/SKILL.md steps 5, 7, 9, 10, 11; core.md planner prompts; the scenarios pool's states in step 5; and scripts/tests plan, which would need to honor a dropped or folded state. Corpus: decision:scenario-list-decided-once says /plan-tests proposes the list, the planners sort every recorded scenario, and the owner approves once; it is silent on how a fix reaches one planner's items. decision:no-execution-engine keeps the tracker from judging, which neither option strains. Harm: cost only (about 4 million tokens for 44 findings across 38 planners, and reviewed scenarios rewritten with changed ids); no accept-list entry. Options: A: a revision refile whose prompt reads the planner's earlier items and the findings and refiles each item unchanged unless a finding names it; cost: a prompt branch and a way to hand the earlier items over, and each finding still costs a planner run. B: the session applies a mechanical finding (rename, drop, fold, a wording fix) with tasks item set, and refiles only for a finding that needs the planner's judgment; cost: the session writes planner output, which widens step 11, needs a dropped state in the scenarios pool that tests plan honors, and needs a rule for which findings count as mechanical. C: both; cost: both. Recommended: C, since B removes the bulk of the cost for the common case and A keeps reviewed scenarios stable when judgment is needed; flip to B alone where the owner wants one new mechanism. Siblings: plan-tests-rejects-a-malformed-scenario-id-only-at-assembly; rule together, since its option B is this issue's option B for a rename.

- i46: discovery-question-on-proposed-artifact-drafts-nothing: Evidence, re-verified, holds as filed. The audit's merge step, plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/discover-design/core.md:404-410, says for an artifact the audit proposes "the stale answer is `new` on that artifact, its body the artifact as the code has it; the wrong answer is the work item that makes the code match the text at issue, with the sentence the artifact records once it does; and no ordinary delta stands beside it". The assembler enforces the last clause: scripts/discover:583 refuses a delta on a proposed artifact ("question %s's stale answer creates the artifact; withdraw the delta"). The planning walk, plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-sprint/SKILL.md:91, says for "The code is wrong": "carry its work item, and the artifact's other delta where the discovery drafts one". For a proposed artifact no other delta exists, so the sprint carries the work item alone and the corpus ends the sprint without the artifact; the wrong answer's sentence is the only draft of it, and nothing tells planning to turn it into a `new` delta. Mechanism: the stale answer's `new` body is the only drafted body for a proposed artifact, and only the stale answer carries it. Corpus: story:bootstrap-design-corpus promises the code read against the corpus is "turned into the corpus changes it needs plus the questions only I can answer"; decision:corpus-audit-hands-a-discovery-to-planning says each question has "both answers: the code is right and the corpus changes, or the corpus is right and the code changes", and that the planning session "drafts each promise change into the sprint"; it is silent on a question about an artifact the corpus does not hold, where "the corpus is right" has no corpus text behind it. decision:final-form-deltas: a delta the audit drafts is a draft until a planning session carries it in final form. Tooling the change would edit: skills/discover-design/core.md Merge step 6 and Record (questions pool fields), scripts/discover (assembler check at :583, question_section's answer lines), and skills/plan-sprint/SKILL.md:91. Harm: under the code-is-wrong answer the sprint fixes the code but the corpus still lacks the artifact the audit found missing, so the story's "corpus changes it needs" go unmade and the next audit proposes the same artifact again; no accept-list entry is needed, this is a judgment issue about tooling. Options: A. The audit drafts a second body per proposed-artifact question, the artifact as the text at issue has it, under answers/<question>/wrong/, and planning carries it as a `new` delta under the code-is-wrong answer; cost: a second full body per such question, a new body path the assembler and question_section must check and show, and the walk text changes. B. Planning drafts the artifact's `new` delta in session from the wrong answer's sentence, and SKILL.md:91 says so; cost: an undrafted body is written in the planning dialogue, outside the audit's review, and the owner reviews prose the audit never checked. C. The code-is-wrong answer carries only the work item, as now, and the corpus records the artifact in a later sprint or audit; cost: the corpus gap stays after the fix, and the walk should say so plainly so the owner knows. A fourth the filer missed: D. The wrong answer's work item names the artifact's `new` delta as part of its own done-state, so the sprint's builder... no: a builder applies only approved deltas, so D collapses into A or B. No stated rule decides among A to C. Siblings: discovery-answer-line-reads-news (retired this run; same question_section code that A touches).
- i47: doc-edit-rules-ignore-reader-and-covers: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-docs/core.md:7-24 ({{DOC-EDIT-RULES}}) lists six rules (false claim; missing public element of a `## Lists` class; internal element shown; a sprint since the stamp changed what a user can do; departure from `## Shape` or the `## Where` layout; unsettleable claim), then core.md:22 "Every other sentence stays as written." No rule names `## Reader` or `## Covers`. The block is transcluded into the planner (core.md:104) and the writer (core.md:197). The filed problem still holds. Mechanism: decision:docspec-stamp-opens-the-window makes a docspec whose "own text" changed since its stamp reach planning, so an Amend-docspec delta to Reader or Covers reaches it; but the planner plans an item only where a rule fires, and none fires on a reader or coverage departure, so the plan holds no item and the stamp moves past the amendment. A docspec first declared over existing documentation is "planned as new", where only claims are checked against the tree, so the same gap holds there. Corpus: story:declare-project-documentation promises a way to declare "whom it is for, and what it describes, so that whoever writes that documentation writes what I asked for"; concept:docspec Purpose: "The docspec also tells the writer whom the text is for, what to cover, what to leave out ... so the text follows the owner's intent instead of the writer's guess." decision:documentation-edits-only-where-a-rule-fires fixes the rule set to exactly the six core.md carries ("Every other sentence stays as written"), so code and that decision agree with each other and both contradict the story's sentence. Harm: A8 (a live story's commitment; the rule decides that some edit rule must fire), and the run reports a docspec current whose documentation departs from its reader and coverage. Compliant corpus change, forced because the decision and the code both contradict the story: amend decision:documentation-edits-only-where-a-rule-fires to add one rule in the shape of its layout rule: "the file departs from its docspec's reader or coverage: it addresses another reader, covers what the docspec leaves out, or omits what it covers" with the edit "rewrite the passage that departs"; the build then adds the matching row to {{DOC-EDIT-RULES}} in core.md. The alternative of re-planning an amended docspec as new does not close the first-declaration case, which is already planned as new. No sibling issue in this batch.
- i48: edit-hook-skips-bash-and-notebook-edits: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/hooks/post-edit.js:41 lintStage reads only `event.tool_input && event.tool_input.file_path` and returns null without one, so a Bash payload (no file_path) and a NotebookEdit payload (its field is notebook_path) are never linted; plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/plumbline:64-91 COMMENT_GRAMMARS has no `.ipynb` entry, so the lint reads no notebook at all. True-up wires the hook as PostToolUse with matcher "" on every tool (admin/true-up:819, :830), so any tool whose input carries file_path is linted, Read included: this is why the driver saw a Read of an untracked file holding a comment exit 2. The cheatsheet source plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/docs/plumbline-cheatsheet.md:161 says "It does nothing for a Bash call." The filed problem holds. Corpus: story:edit-time-lint-enforcement wants "every agent edit checked against the lint checks my project turned on as it lands"; decision:edit-hook-blocks-in-turn chooses "a post-edit hook ... only within the edited file's changed line ranges for tracked files", with failure paths degrading to a silent pass, and is silent on which tools count as edits. The review loop's checks (.ok-planner/review/config.json checks: `node .ok-planner/bin/plumbline`) lint changed files at review time, which catches Bash edits later, not as they land. Options: A. Keep the story's "every agent edit": the decision widens the hook to lint every file git reports changed after a Bash or NotebookEdit call (changed ranges as now), and the lint gains a notebook grammar. Cost: a git status and diff after every Bash call, a slower hook, and edits by other processes attributed to the agent's turn. B. Narrow the story to edits through the editing tools (Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit), the decision names that scope, and Bash edits fall to the review-time lint. Cost: residue written through Bash lands unchecked until review. C (the filer missed): B, plus the hook reads notebook_path so NotebookEdit is checked, and the lint reads code cells. Cost: the lint must parse notebook JSON. Whatever the ruling, the build should restrict the wired matcher or lintStage to the editing tools so a Read no longer lints and blocks; that Read behavior is a separate defect class the author may note. No sibling issue in this batch.
- i49: confirm-drive-per-defect-or-per-story: Evidence, re-verified: the tooling is built as option A. plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/scripts/review:confirm_briefs (1291-1299) files one brief per defect whose story field lists every story (defect_stories, 1284-1287); plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/SKILL.md:116 says `review drives --confirm` "files one confirm driver per defect the dry run listed"; plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/converge/prompts/drive.md:60-63 says a confirm brief naming several stories drives each in turn, marks the defect confirmed only on "achieved, on every story the brief names", and sends it back on any other outcome on any story. The project.md entry for `drives --confirm --dry-run` still prints `{"pending": [{"defect", "story"}]}`, singular story. Mechanism: a merge may fold two drive failures with one cause on different stories into one defect, and the `confirmed` field lives on the defect, so per-story drivers would race on one mark: one driver confirms while another sends back, and after the refix the stale confirmed mark stops the defect from being confirmed again. Corpus: decision:drive-tries-each-story-as-a-user says drive mode and sprint certification "each give every story its own driver once per run", which governs the drive, not the confirm, and the corpus says nothing of the confirm drive's unit. story:find-and-fix-defects only promises defects "found and fixed without me". Options: A. One confirm driver per defect drives every story the defect names and gives one verdict, as built. Cost: one driver carries several stories' drives, a longer task, and its verdict hides which story failed unless its note says. B. One confirm driver per story, and a defect is confirmed only when every story's driver confirms. Cost: confirmed becomes a per-story set on the defect, review drives and the drive prompt change, and the stale-mark race needs the mark cleared on every send-back. Recommend A: it needs no change, keeps one verdict per defect as the fix loop counts send-backs per defect, and the flip case is a run where folded defects often confirm on one story and fail on the other. No sibling issue in this batch.

- i38: ok-outcome-after-declined-second-plan: Evidence, re-verified: plugins/ok/skills/ok/SKILL.md:60 (step 4.5) answers an abort of the first plan with 'write nothing and ask nothing else. Skip steps 5 and 6, and report the outcome declined; stays on v<stamped>'. SKILL.md:72 (step 5.4, as the fixer built it) answers an abort of the second plan with 'write nothing more and go on to step 6; the report lists each DESTRUCTIVE: line the owner turned down, and the outcome reads trued up; plan steps pending: <d>'; SKILL.md:129 repeats that outcome. The filed facts hold. Mechanism: pass one has already applied and re-stamped the layer before step 5 runs, so 'stays on v<stamped>' after a second decline would name the new version while implying nothing changed; and a second plan turns destructive in two named cases (an answer unblocks a destructive step, or an answer or amend draft changes a file pass one rendered, e.g. a lint_checks repair, which archives and rewrites each such file). A decline leaves those files as pass one rendered them, out of step with the answer just applied. Corpus: decision:true-up-asks-once-before-destructive-steps says 'On abort, true-up writes nothing, and the project stays on the suite version its stamps record' and 'All of the plan or none of it are the two states that work', and that the input questions and the wiring come after the plan runs; it is silent on a destructive plan that a post-plan answer causes. story:true-up-project-estate promises one deliberate act that never costs the owner work they wrote. Harm: none an entry covers today beyond a possible A9 report if the outcome claimed 'stays on' the old version. Options: A (as built): report trued up with the declined steps pending and run the wiring; cost: the pass ends with an answer applied to config but not to the files it renders, a part-applied state the decision's rationale warns against, until the next /ok. B: report the first plan's outcome and skip the wiring; cost: the outcome reads as unchanged though pass one's writes and stamps stand (a false report under A9's terms), and the owner loses the wiring consent the decline did not concern. C (missed by the filer): on a decline of the second plan, back out the answer or amend draft that made it destructive, so config and rendered files agree, then report the answer as declined and run the wiring; cost: one more core step, and the owner's answer is lost until the next /ok. Each option needs a sentence added to decision:true-up-asks-once-before-destructive-steps naming the second plan, so this is a promise change. Recommended: A, with the decision delta, since pass one's writes are real, the pending line tells the owner what is owed, and the next /ok re-asks; flip to C where the owner rejects ending a pass with config and rendered files out of step. Siblings: none in this batch.
- i39: plan-tests-reviews-a-whole-plan-with-one-agent: Evidence holds. plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-tests/SKILL.md:66 (step 9) files one review task, 'tasks file --role review --prompt review --agent ok-opus --key review --brief "review the plan"', under {{TEST-PLAN-REVIEW-PROMPT}} at plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-tests/core.md:336-380, whose Check list mixes per-planner checks (no story way yields two scenarios for one program, core.md:357-359; outcome text; reach through a public entry point; port/adopt) with plan-wide ones (owner answers hold, core.md:362-363). Planning is split one planner per story plus one runtime planner; review is not, so the reviewer's reading grows with the plan (linescout, v28.0.0: 485 scenarios, 108 planners, 345 calls, ~538k tokens, 44 findings over ~38 planners). Mechanism: each finding refiles the planner its site names, so one late plan-wide review sends most planners back in one wave after all planning is done. Corpus: silent on how the plan's review is split; scenario-list-decided-once says only that the owner 'approves the whole list once'; tests-check-scenarios and legacy-suites-sorted-automatically ('Sort agents read the tests in batches') bound what is reviewed, not the review's shape. Tooling the change edits: plan-tests SKILL.md step 9 and core.md's review prompt (and the planner prompts for option C). No accept-list entry; a judgment on the project's own tooling, no stated rule decides it. Options: A, one review task per planner plus one plan-wide task for cross-planner checks (duplicates, owner answers): bounded reading per task, more tasks and a second assembly of plan-wide findings; B, review in fixed-size batches of related stories: fewer tasks, but a batch still mixes planners and the batch size is arbitrary; C, move per-planner checks into each planner's prompt as a self-check before close, keep one plan-wide review: cheapest, but a self-check is the planner judging its own work, which a cold reviewer exists to avoid; also missed by the filer, A combined with C. Recommended lean: A, since it matches how planning is already split. Rule with plan-tests-caps-each-story-way-at-one-scenario-per-program (its cap is the check behind most findings; changing it changes what any split review checks) and plan-tests-approval-shows-the-whole-plan-unsorted (same large-plan scale).
- i40: plan-tests-caps-each-story-way-at-one-scenario-per-program: Evidence holds. plugins/ok/families/ok-planner/skills/plan-tests/core.md:27-28 (the scenario definition): 'Each story's way of giving its benefit yields at most one scenario per program that carries it'; core.md:357-359 (plan review): 'No story way yields two scenarios for one program.' The cap is a corpus commitment, not only skill text: decision:tests-check-scenarios, Choice: 'Each story way yields at most one scenario per program that carries it, and each pairing of part, class, and harm yields one'; its Rationale ties the cap to a bounded suite ('bounded by the stories and the runtime parts, not by how many tests an agent thinks to write') and 'A second test of a covered scenario is a duplicate; the test sprint deletes both'. So option A changes what the corpus commits to and needs a corpus delta to that decision, not only a skill edit; the filer frames it as tooling. Mechanism: a planner that files a refusal, a variant input, or a second path through one program as its own scenario departs from the definition, the review flags it, and the session refiles the planner to fold or drop it (linescout, v28.0.0: 26 of 44 findings; e.g. a last-administrator refusal, four liveness states, six provenance checks on one record command). Harm the filer names: distinct outcomes merged into one test or left untested; no accept-list entry covers it (prose and plan shape), it is the owner's choice. Options: A, replace the cap with one scenario per distinct outcome a user or the product sees through a program, keeping only the rule against two scenarios checking one outcome: covers refusals and variants as their own scenarios; cost: the suite grows with outcomes rather than ways, weakening the 'bounded' rationale, and 'distinct outcome' needs a test a reviewer can apply; edits decision:tests-check-scenarios, core.md:27-28 and :357-359, and the planner prompts; B, keep the cap and let one scenario's test check each variant and refusal as a separate case inside it: no corpus change; cost: a scenario's text must then list its cases, and one failing case marks the whole scenario failing, so the test loop's per-scenario issue wait (scenario-list-decided-once: 'the open issue a failing scenario waits on') covers several outcomes at once; C (missed by the filer), keep the cap per way but count a refusal the story names as its own way: smallest change, but only covers refusals, not variants or states. Rule with plan-tests-reviews-a-whole-plan-with-one-agent (this cap drives most of that review's findings) and plan-tests-approval-shows-the-whole-plan-unsorted.

Options: A, a drop verb that appends a removal event (who, why) and hides the item from later reads: one verb, every reader benefits, record kept; cost: a new event type in the run file format and the index rebuild; B, a 'dropped' state per pool that every reader skips, set through the existing item set: no new verb, but every reader (the tests assembler at tests:514, 521, 530, 532, 749, 1048, 1096; review; docs) must learn to skip it, and a reader that forgets reads a dropped item; C (missed by the filer), have the assembler refuse with a per-item message and let the session refile only the one planner with its failure in the brief, as SKILL.md step 7 already does: no tracker change, but it keeps the rerun cost the issue names.
